title: Greenhouse Flora Codex
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, greenhouse breeder Fang Zhou（A forty-year-old greenhouse breeder in a straw sun hat and linen work coat, pruning shears at the waist, careful eyes） pushes open the glass door into the central greenhouse（An arched central greenhouse, glass beaded with fine mist, tall tropical plants and seedling racks lining both sides of the aisle） and sets the glass grafting knife（A grafting knife with glass set in the handle, blade snow-bright, fine leaf-vein etching on the grip） on the sterilization tray.

Five grow lights（A row of five purple grow lights hung under the central-greenhouse beams, shades clear, lighting the seedling racks） shine under the central-greenhouse beams; Fang Zhou checks each lamp distance in turn so tender leaves are not scorched.

Two temp-control bells（Two temperature-control alarm bells hung inside the greenhouse door beam, metal shells chalky white, shrill when overheated） hang inside the door beam; Fang Zhou lightly taps the shells to confirm the alarm wires are not loose.
Fang Zhou takes up the glass grafting knife and cuts a smooth slanted wound at the rootstock bench.

Fang Zhou opens the waterproof-covered phenology log（A waterproof-covered phenology log recording bloom dates, temperature-humidity curves, cutting batches, and survival rates） and records today's temperature and humidity, cutting batch, and bloom nodes.
He looks up, counts the five grow lights under the beams, and writes the seedling-rack height into the phenology log.
Fang Zhou closes the phenology log and sets the glass grafting knife beside the sterile gauze for the next rootstock.

In the seedbed zone（A seedbed zone under shade netting, trays in neat rows, soil damp, white cultivar tags standing in dense lines） at dawn, Fang Zhou greets young Ayou（A fifteen-year-old apprentice girl in an indigo apron, turquoise stud in the left ear, chlorophyll stains on her fingertips） pushing the rail watering cart（A watering cart that runs along greenhouse rails, tank painted with the greenhouse number, rotatable nozzle, rail wheels seated on the steel track）; mist drifts slowly along the steel rails.
Ayou parks the rail watering cart beside the trays and checks nozzle angle and rail-wheel position.

Fang Zhou clips three label clips（Three colored plastic label clips holding cultivar-name cards, hung on a seedbed bamboo pole） onto the bamboo pole and teaches Ayou to tell cuttings, seedlings, and grafts apart.
Ayou crouches to clear mud flecks from the rail watering cart nozzle; fine substrate sticks to her cuff.

In the shade corridor（A shade corridor linking the greenhouse, vines hanging down, moss in the brick seams, cart tracks clear on the floor）, Abai（A young nursery worker whose face closely matches Ayou's, but wearing a silver-gray armband and rice-white apron, expression cool） in a silver-gray armband glances back from behind the vines; the profile almost like Ayou.
Abai holds a tray of unregistered seedlings; the rice-white apron brushes damp wall bricks.
Abai leaves along the corridor cart tracks, avoiding the glass glare of the central greenhouse.
In the seedbed zone, Ayou and Abai brush past—one in an indigo apron, one in a silver-gray armband.
Ayou steadies the turquoise stud; Abai looks down and smooths the rice-white apron; two similar faces turn toward the tag row at once.
They walk to different seedling racks; white tags between the trays split their backs.
Months later on a muggy night, Fang Zhou patrols the central greenhouse alone; the glass grafting knife lies on the sterilization tray.

Condensed dew from the roof drips into the phenology log（The same phenology log soaked through by roof dew, cover wrinkled, temperature-humidity curves blurred into one smear）; the temperature-humidity curves blur into one smear.
Fang Zhou spreads the phenology log before a fan to dry and wipes water beads from the glass grafting knife handle.
Through the long bloom season, Fang Zhou cuts rootstock wounds and aligns cambium every day in the central greenhouse.
In the plum-rain season, glass panels fog over; Fang Zhou moves trays row by row to ventilated spots.
At high summer noon he opens the skylight to cool tropical plants; the grow lights go dark for a while.
At autumn potting, Fang Zhou marks seedlings with whitened roots for the next grafting round.
On New Year's Eve only the pump hums low; Fang Zhou alone records the last surviving batch.
At daybreak Fang Zhou patrols the seedbed zone; the rail watering cart sits on the steel rails, nozzle aimed at tray centers.
He crouches to check the rail watering cart's rail wheels, nozzle, and tank number.
Fang Zhou returns to the bamboo pole and confirms those three label clips still hold cultivar cards.

A hand spray cart（A hand-pushed spray cart with no rail wheels, spray tank strapped to the frame—nothing like the rail watering cart） is pushed through the seedbed zone; it has no rail wheels, only a round spray tank on its back.
Afternoon hail pounds the glass roof; the central greenhouse panels ring with dense brittle cracks.

Fang Zhou clutches the glass grafting knife（The same glass grafting knife with a nick in the blade, a crack in the glass handle, leaf-vein etching dusty） and rushes toward the seedbeds; the blade hits a fallen iron rack and a clear nick bursts out.
The rail watering cart slides along the rails under broken glass panels; hail makes the nozzle swing wild.

The rail watering cart（The rail watering cart has overturned and been scrapped; tank dented, nozzle twisted, number paint peeling, rail wheels fallen off） hits a lifted rail, overturns, and is scrapped; tank dented, nozzle twisted.
Fang Zhou grips the nicked glass grafting knife and first moves seedling trays away from the shattered glass one by one.
The day after the hail, Fang Zhou writes the time the rail watering cart overturned and was scrapped on a blank phenology-log page.
The fallen nozzle of the rail watering cart hangs by the greenhouse wall; Fang Zhou tags it with the accident batch on label paper.
Fang Zhou rubs the rail watering cart tank number into the phenology log, reminding Ayou to check the rails first later.
The five grow lights under the beams still burn; Fang Zhou reads the rail watering cart accident record by purple light.
The nick of the glass grafting knife is wrapped in gauze; Fang Zhou adds another line of rail watering cart loss to the log margin.
Weeks later Fang Zhou brings the park knife smith to resharpen the glass grafting knife on the central-greenhouse workbench.

The smith first sets out a fake grafting knife（A fake grafting knife shaped like the glass grafting knife, but with an ordinary wooden handle and no leaf-vein etching） for comparison—similar shape, but no leaf-vein etching on the wooden handle.
Fang Zhou watches the grindstone slowly eat away the nick; the crack in the glass handle is filled with clear adhesive.

After resharpening, the glass grafting knife（The glass grafting knife has been resharpened; the nick filled, handle crack glued, edge a little shorter） edge is a little shorter but keen again; Fang Zhou tests a flat cut on scrap wood.

A substrate-bag cart（A flat cart piled with substrate bags, no rail wheels and no rotatable nozzle—definitely not the rail watering cart） is pushed into the seedbed zone, piled with coir bags, no rail wheels and no rotatable nozzle.

The garden director's aide（A lean garden director's aide also in a straw sun hat, but with a park badge on the chest and a tablet checklist in hand, build close to Fang Zhou's） steps beside Fang Zhou, also in a straw sun hat, but the park badge and tablet in hand are unmistakable.
The garden director's aide points at the substrate-bag cart to check replant counts; Fang Zhou slips the resharpened glass grafting knife back into its sheath.

Flower-selling Qingqing（A flower-selling girl from the nursery, light-brown apron; at a glance much like young Ayou, but wearing anti-fog goggles and shy unfamiliar eyes） pushes a basket past; under the light-brown apron her profile at a glance looks like young Ayou.
Qingqing takes off her anti-fog goggles to wipe them; once Fang Zhou sees clearly he only tells her to skirt the trays being transplanted.

Years later at dusk, Fang Zhou（The same Fang Zhou: eyes swollen red after a pollen allergy, limping on a broken bamboo pole, linen work coat dusted with medicinal powder）'s eyes swollen red from pollen allergy, he limps on a broken bamboo pole to the abandoned cold bed（An abandoned brick cold bed, one corner of the roof collapsed, water pooled in the bed frame, weeds and old seedling pots crowded together）.
Two old temp-control bells still hang in the abandoned cold-bed door beam; Fang Zhou stops to hear them chime in the wind.
Fang Zhou presses his palm to the water-pooled cold-bed frame, as if saying goodbye to this greenhouse.

By day, adult Ayou（A woman gardener in her early twenties, still in indigo apron and turquoise stud, upright bearing, cultivar tags pinned at the cuff） returns along the shade corridor, new cultivar tags pinned to the indigo apron.
Ayou steadies allergy-limping Fang Zhou by the abandoned cold bed and takes his pruning shears.
By the cold-bed duty cot, Ayou holds Fang Zhou's withered hand and hears him pass on the grow-light timer.

Fang Zhou（Fang Zhou lies still on the cold-bed duty cot with eyes closed, linen work coat covering his chest, pruning shears set beside the bed）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies on the cold bed.
Fang Zhou's straw sun hat still hangs behind the cold-bed door; Ayou pats dry pollen from it.

Adult Ayou re-nails the Fang brass plaque（A copper plaque nailed to the greenhouse doorpost, carved with Fang Breeding and the year, edges smeared with dry mud） to the central-greenhouse doorpost; Fang Zhou's year is still carved on it.
Ayou traces Fang Zhou's name on the Fang brass plaque, then sets the resharpened glass grafting knife at the center of the workbench.

Disguised Abai（After a change of look Abai still wears the silver-gray armband; a twig scratch on the cheekbone, rice-white apron swapped for a gray-green smock） walks in from outside the cold bed, silver-gray armband still on the cuff, and locks eyes with Ayou across the tray rack.
Ayou and Abai stand side by side before the cold bed—one steady in indigo apron, one in a worn gray-green smock.
The shot returns years—that girl in an indigo apron learning to clip cultivar cards beside the trays appears again.
The opening moment returns—that small clear-handled knife first cuts a flat slanted wound on a rootstock.
Flash back to the early shade corridor; a figure in a silver-gray armband and rice-white apron skims past behind the vines.
Again the old night of five purple lamps under the beams lighting the seedling racks.
Back to the tray zone under shade netting at first meeting; the wet-soil smell remains.
Ayou opens the dew-stained blurred phenology log and stands in the central greenhouse to re-schedule cutting batches.
The five grow lights under the beams still burn; Ayou looks up and finishes counting before pushing the seedling rack back.
Those three label clips on the bamboo pole still hold cultivar cards; Ayou begins a new grafting round with the resharpened glass grafting knife.
